messages:
maya (support): FYI customer SUP-4598 on a Private deployment experiencing 502s from their API gateway since ~01:00 UTC. They see TLS handshake failures and timeouts. Customer says this started right after our peering maintenance. Can someone take a look?
customer-ops: attaching snippets from the customer: `curl -v https://api.private.example` -> `* SSL: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate`
customer-ops: openssl output: `openssl s_client -connect api.private.example:443 -showcerts` -> `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate` and only server cert present (no intermediate). Also DNS: `dig api.private.example +short` -> `10.10.20.5` (we were expecting 10.20.30.5 after peering swap).
eli (net-eng): thanks. Two immediate possibilities: (1) DNS still resolving to old peering IP (BGP/route propagation) and that path goes via transit firewall with different TLS termination (missing intermediate cert), or (2) our edge gateway lost the intermediate cert during automated rotation.
eli (net-eng): can you ask customer to `curl --resolve 'api.private.example:443:10.20.30.5' https://api.private.example/health --insecure` to see if endpoint at new IP responds (bypass their DNS). Also `traceroute -n 10.10.20.5` and `traceroute -n 10.20.30.5` would help.
sophie (oncall): incident-bot assigned to oncall (sophie). I see the automated cert rotation pipeline ran at 01:07 UTC for this tenant. Need to check edge gateways (haproxy/nginx) for fullchain vs cert only.
support-lead: if this impacts production traffic for >1 customer, escalate to eng-sre and open an incident. Keep SUP-4598 updated.
eli (net-eng): quick check commands for us: on edge gateway `openssl x509 -text -noout -in /etc/ssl/certs/server.crt | grep "Issuer\|Subject"` and `cat /etc/ssl/certs/fullchain.pem | wc -l` to ensure intermediate included. Also check BGP table: `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast' | grep 10.20.30.0/24` and `ip route get 10.10.20.5` on leaf routers.
maya (support): customer ran `curl --resolve 'api.private.example:443:10.20.30.5'` and got a 200 OK and proper JSON; they claim errors only when their DNS resolves to 10.10.20.5. They attached a pcap showing TLS ClientHello to 10.10.20.5 then server sends `Alert (unknown CA)`.
eli (net-eng): that confirms two things: new service on 10.20.30.5 is healthy and serving full chain; old path (10.10.20.5) is going to a transit device that either terminates TLS with a wrong cert or strips intermediates. Likely firewall WAF/proxy in DC using old cert bundle.
sophie (oncall): I see in the deployment logs the certificate rotation job updated `server.crt` but a separate script that generates `fullchain.pem` failed on one node (node-edge-3) due to transient file lock. That node is still advertising 10.10.20.5 via BGP for that tenant.
eli (net-eng): plan: 1) update node-edge-3 with correct fullchain.pem and reload proxy (haproxy/nginx) -> immediate fix for TLS chain; 2) ensure BGP withdraw/advertise to move routes to 10.20.30.5 only; 3) as mitigation add customer's client IP ranges (or the peering ranges) to firewall egress allowlist if packets are being dropped.
support-lead: can net-eng patch node-edge-3 now? Customer is at 40% error rate.
eli (net-eng): pushing a quick fix now: `scp fullchain.pem node-edge-3:/etc/ssl/certs/ && ssh node-edge-3 'systemctl reload haproxy'` (will monitor).
incident-bot: Assigned to eli (net-eng) and sophie (oncall). Incident ID INC-2025 created and linked to SUP-4598.
maya (support): customer reports errors drop to ~2% after reload, but intermittent DNS still returns 10.10.20.5 for some of their clients. Could be cached DNS or multiple peering prefixes still advertised.
eli (net-eng): I'm checking BGP: looks like node-edge-3 withdrew 10.10.20.5 route but the route is still present in upstream transit router because of stale route reflector entry. I'll force a soft-reconfig and clear route-reflector cache.
sophie (oncall): running `vtysh -c 'clear bgp * soft in'` on RR cluster now. Also asking infra to check route-reflector logs for sourcing.
maya (support): customer confirms propagation improving, DNS now resolves to 10.20.30.5 for most clients. They asked about the root cause — can we confirm?
eli (net-eng): root cause summary: automated cert rotation missed including intermediate on node-edge-3 due to file lock -> node served incomplete chain at 10.10.20.5. Simultaneously BGP/route-reflector stale entry kept the old peering IP advertised for a subset of clients -> traffic hit the bad node. Fixes: re-upload fullchain, reload proxy, clear RR cache.
support-lead: please add postmortem blameless note and follow-up to enhance rotation job to verify fullchain presence and to add a preflight BGP withdraw check.
sophie (oncall): filing follow-up tasks: - rotation pipeline: verify `openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt /etc/ssl/certs/fullchain.pem` as step - RR: improved convergence test after peering change - add an alert if error rate for tenant > 5% after rotation
maya (support): customer happy for now, reduced errors to single-digit and agreed to scheduled validation window. Closing SUP-4598 once postmortem sent. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
customer-ops: thanks team, appreciate the quick turn around :pray:
eli (net-eng): adding annotations to INC-2025 with commands and timeline.
